episodes.172849: An upper level trough had moved into the Central Plains. An upper level disturbance associated with the upper trough moved over West Texas. This helped increase lift over the area. Low-level moisture was also fairly high across the area. These conditions resulted in storms that produced severe wind gusts and flash flooding across parts of West Texas.
episodes.173129: A cold front moved through southern New England during the early evening triggering a few severe thunderstorms in northern Massachusetts.
episodes.173294: Pre-frontal convection pressed southward across northeast Florida ahead of a stalling cold front. Some storms produced gusty winds.
episodes.173695: An active pattern in mid-September resulted in several reports of flash flooding in southern Utah, in addition to some isolated thunderstorm related wind gusts in northern Utah.
episodes.174045: A trough just to the west of Arizona and southerly flow aloft helped produce scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced large hail, funnel clouds, and small tornadoes.
episodes.174258: A slow moving low brought scattered thunderstorms to the region. Most thunderstorms carried gusty winds and small hail. One thunderstorm recorded one inch hail.
episodes.174540: A rain shower caused a localized microburst that brought severe wind gusts to the Casper-Natrona County Airport. No damage was reported. This wind magnitude is common for this area.
episodes.174570: A line of convection developed from central to southern New Hampshire ahead of an approaching cold front on the evening of September 13th.  The line became severe across southern New Hampshire and began to bow out bringing damaging wind gusts to Hillsbourgh County.
episodes.174608: The remnant circulation of former Pacific Hurricane Kay brought thunderstorms and flash flooding to the Mojave Desert.

events.narrative: Hwy 93 was flooded at Lincoln Co mile markers 105 and 109.
Knee high mud was over Hwy 190, and a school bus was stuck in the mud.
Convective outflow winds associated with a line of severe thunderstorms downed trees and wires in Greenfield.
Convective outflow winds associated with a line of severe thunderstorms downed tress and large branches at Woodland Hill Rd. in Greenfield.
In Ashby trees were down on Flint Rd, West Rd, and Jewett Hill Rd.
Convective outflow winds associated with a line of severe thunderstorms downed trees in the Mount Vernon area. A home weather station reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.
A tornado formed and traveled along the leading edge of a thunderstorm outflow boundary.
There were multiple reports of flooding in Alamo.
Hwy 6 was flooded with water and mud.

Significant road flooding occurred in Moapa, Moapa Valley, Overton, and Valley of Fire State Park. The Overton co-op observer measured 1.89 inches of rain, including 0.80 inch in 20 minutes. Multiple vehicles were stuck in Valley of Fire.
No lightning was detected in the area, so this was technically not a thunderstorm at the time of the severe wind observation.
Thunderstorm recorded one inch hail. It formed South of Lake Omak around 1835PST and moved North toward Omak. It lasted until 1940PST. Time is estimated by radar. No damage or injuries reported.

events.location: 8.05 NW Las Vegas N Air Term
events.narrative: The intersection of Farm Rd and Grand Canyon Dr was flooded.

Moderate to heavy rainfall from earlier in the day resulted in a flood wave traversing downstream along the Virgin River. The Virgin at Virgin river gauge recorded a flow increase from 333 CFS at 12:15 am MST to a peak of 2020 CFS at 2:00 am MST.
A thunderstorm produced a 63 mph wind gust at the Kent Mesonet site.
A thunderstorm produced a 60 mph wind gust at the Coyanosa Mesonet site.

events.county: St Augustine To Flagler Beach Fl Out 20Nm
events.narrative: A spotter measured a wind gust of 40 mph about 2 miles north of Flagler Beach. The nearest thunderstorm was 10-15 miles offshore of Flagler Beach.
